correctness.rationale: Every set with at least two vertices dominates CP_n since each vertex has one distinct non-neighbor, forcing the zero set of a maximal double Roman function to have at most one vertex. With no zero, weight <=2n+1 leaves a sole defender 2 and its partner as an undefended 1. With exactly one zero, a baseline 2n-1 on positive vertices needs two more units. The sole-3 possibility fails at that 3-vertex partner; exactly two adjacent 2-defenders achieve equality. Independent exhaustive labelings n=2..4 recovered (value,count) (5,4),(7,36),(9,120); n>=2 generality comes from proof.

value.rationale: Cocktail party graphs are the canonical complete graphs minus a perfect matching, and the minimality/maximality interplay forces an unusually rigid complete classification of all optimal functions, not just a parameter count.

final_claim: For n>=2, maximal double Roman domination number of CP_n=K_{2,...,2} is 2n+1. Every optimal labeling has exactly one 0, its nonadjacent partner has 1, exactly two vertices not in that pair have 2, others 1; precisely 2n C(2n-2,2) minima.
limitations: n>=2; the zero set must be nondominating in closed-neighborhood sense.
Independent enumeration n<=4 corroborates, but is not the infinite proof.
